subject: Mathematics
board: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE (9–1) Mathematics A (4MA1), Higher tier
source: School Maths folder: Pearson International GCSE Mathematics A (4MA1) two-year Scheme of Work, Higher course order (Unit 16 Harder graphs and transformations of graphs; Unit 17 Simultaneous equations); 2024 4MA1 Paper 1H for exam style; INSET lesson standard.

lessons.unit: Unit 16: Harder graphs and transformations of graphs
lessons.title: Quadratic graphs: roots, turning points and symmetry
lessons.bigQuestion: What can the shape of a quadratic graph tell us without plotting every point?
objectives: Plot quadratic graphs from a table of values
Identify roots, y-intercept, turning point and line of symmetry
Use a graph to solve a quadratic equation
successCriteria: Complete a table and plot y = x² − 2x − 3
Read roots, turning point and line of symmetry from the graph
Find the turning point by completing the square and compare with the graph
lessons.crossCurricular: Physics: the path of a projectile; Business: maximising profit
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: the symmetry in the arc of a thrown ball, water from a fountain

keywords.def: the U-shaped curve of a quadratic graph
where the graph crosses the x-axis: a solution of y = 0
the minimum or maximum point of the curve
the vertical line through the turning point

starter: What is the y-intercept of y = 2x + 5?

teach.heading: Table of values
bullets: Plot and join with a smooth curve
teach.note: Model on graph paper on screen. Stress: never join with straight lines or a pointed bottom.

teach.heading: Reading key features
bullets: Line of symmetry: x = 1, halfway between the roots
teach.note: Ask: 'Why is the line of symmetry halfway between the roots?' Because the parabola is symmetrical.

teach.heading: Turning point by completing the square
bullets: (x + p)² + q has turning point (−p, q)
teach.note: Model.

model.problem: Find the turning point of y = x² − 2x − 3

teach.heading: Sign error with negative x
teach.note: Most table errors come from this.

teach.heading: Check: features
teach.note: Show me on 3.

check.q: A parabola has roots at x = −4 and x = 2. What is its line of symmetry?
check.why: Halfway between −4 and 2: (−4 + 2)/2 = −1. A halves −4; C uses (4 − 2)/2.

practice: Complete a table for y = x² + x − 6 for −4 ≤ x ≤ 3
Find the roots from your graph
Write down the y-intercept and line of symmetry
independent: Core: Plot y = x² − 4x + 1 for −1 ≤ x ≤ 5. Use it to solve x² − 4x + 1 = 0 to 1 d.p.
Extend: Write x² − 6x + 5 in the form (x − p)² − q, state the turning point, and sketch the graph showing all intercepts.
Stretch: A ball's height is h = 20t − 5t². Find when it lands and its maximum height. Show the maximum height using completing the square.
exit: Roots of y = (x − 2)(x + 6)?
Line of symmetry of that graph?
Turning point of y = (x + 3)² − 7?
lessons.homework: 4MA1 Higher graph questions: complete the table, draw the graph and use it to solve two equations.
lessons.send: Support: tables partly completed. Stretch: maximum-value problems.

lessons.unit: Unit 16: Harder graphs and transformations of graphs
lessons.title: Cubic and reciprocal graphs
lessons.bigQuestion: Why does the graph of y = 1/x never touch the axes?
successCriteria: Complete tables and plot y = x³ − 3x
Plot y = 1/x and describe its asymptotes
Sketch and match graphs of linear, quadratic, cubic and reciprocal functions
lessons.crossCurricular: Science: Boyle's law (pressure and volume) is a reciprocal relationship
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: approaching but never reaching: a picture of infinity

keywords.def: a function whose highest power is x³
a function of the form y = k/x
a line the graph gets closer and closer to but never meets
a neat graph showing the shape and key points, not to scale

teach.heading: Cubic graphs
teach.note: Plot y = x³ − 3x from x = −2 to 2: y = −2, 2, 0, −2, 2.

teach.heading: Reciprocal graphs
teach.note: Answer the big question: x can never be 0, and 1/x is never exactly 0 however large x gets.

misconception.right: x = 0 is undefined: the graph never touches the axes

teach.heading: Matching shapes
bullets: Recognise the family by its highest power or x in the denominator
teach.note: Display four sketches and match: straight line, U-shape, S-shape, two branches.

teach.heading: Check: identify the graph
teach.note: Show me on 3.

check.q: A graph has two branches, in the first and third quadrants, and never meets the axes. Its equation could be…
check.why: Reciprocal graphs y = k/x with k > 0 lie in quadrants 1 and 3. The others are continuous curves or lines through the origin.

practice: Complete a table for y = x³ for −3 ≤ x ≤ 3
Complete a table for y = 6/x for x = 1, 2, 3, 6
independent: Core: Plot y = x³ − 4x for −3 ≤ x ≤ 3 and find its roots
Extend: Plot y = 12/x for 1 ≤ x ≤ 12 and use it to estimate x when y = 5. Check by calculation.
Stretch: Sketch y = x³ − x² − 6x by factorising first. Show where it crosses the axes.
exit: Name the shape of y = 2x³
Write the asymptotes of y = 5/x
Sketch y = x² and y = x³ on the same axes
lessons.homework: 4MA1 Higher: match ten equations to sketches, and plot one reciprocal graph.
lessons.send: Support: graph-family cards. Stretch: exponential graphs y = aˣ.

lessons.unit: Unit 16: Harder graphs and transformations of graphs
lessons.title: Using graphs to solve equations
lessons.bigQuestion: How can drawing one straight line solve a hard equation?
objectives: Solve equations using the intersection of two graphs
Rearrange an equation to find the line to draw
successCriteria: Solve x² − 2x − 3 = 0 from a graph
Solve x² − 2x − 3 = 2 using y = 2
Find the line to draw to solve x² − 4x + 1 = 0 using the graph of y = x² − 3x
lessons.crossCurricular: Science: graphical analysis of experimental data
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: two different paths meeting at one truth

keywords.def: the point where two graphs cross
a value that makes the equation true
an approximate reading from a graph
change the form of the equation

starter: Where does y = x² − 4 cross the x-axis?

teach.heading: Reading solutions
bullets: f(x) = 0: where the curve meets the x-axis
f(x) = k: where it meets the line y = k
teach.note: On the y = x² − 2x − 3 graph, draw y = 2. Read x ≈ −1.4 and 3.4.

teach.heading: Finding the line to draw
bullets: Rearrange so one side is the plotted graph
The other side is the line
teach.note: Model.

model.problem: The graph of y = x² − 3x is drawn. What line solves x² − 4x + 1 = 0?
steps: We want x² − 3x on the left
Read the x-values where the line meets the curve

teach.heading: Reading y instead of x
teach.note: Pupils often give the y-coordinate of the intersection.

misconception.right: Solutions are the x-coordinates: x ≈ −1.4 and 3.4

teach.heading: Check: which line?
teach.note: Show me on 3.

check.q: The graph of y = x² is drawn. Which line solves x² − 2x − 1 = 0?
check.why: x² = 2x + 1. B has the signs reversed; D gets the constant wrong.

practice: From the y = x² − 2x − 3 graph, solve x² − 2x − 3 = −3
Read the solutions from the graph
independent: Core: Draw y = x² − x − 2 for −2 ≤ x ≤ 3 and solve (a) x² − x − 2 = 0 (b) x² − x − 2 = 3
Extend: Using the graph of y = x³ − 3x, solve x³ − 3x = 1 to 1 d.p.
Stretch: Using the graph of y = x² + 2x, find the line to draw to solve 2x² + x − 5 = 0, and solve it.
exit: What do the solutions of f(x) = 0 look like on a graph?
Graph y = x² drawn. Which line solves x² − 5 = 0?
Give the solutions as x or y values?
lessons.homework: 4MA1 Higher 'use your graph to solve' questions (four items) with full workings.
lessons.send: Support: pre-drawn graphs. Stretch: simultaneous equations by graph.

lessons.unit: Unit 16: Harder graphs and transformations of graphs
lessons.title: Transformations of graphs: translations
lessons.bigQuestion: Why does f(x + 2) move a graph to the left, not the right?
objectives: Sketch y = f(x) + a and y = f(x + a)
successCriteria: Sketch y = f(x) + 3 from y = f(x)
Sketch y = f(x − 2) and describe the translation as a vector
Find the new coordinates of a turning point after a translation
lessons.crossCurricular: Computing: moving sprites by coordinates; Art: transforming designs
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: the same shape in a new place; constancy amid change

keywords.def: f(x) means the output of function f for input x
a slide without turning or resizing
a column showing a movement (right/left over up/down)
unchanged by a transformation

teach.heading: Up and down: f(x) + a
teach.note: Show y = x² and y = x² + 3 on the same axes. Turning point (0, 0) → (0, 3).

teach.heading: Left and right: f(x + a)
teach.note: Answer the big question: for f(x + 2) to equal f(0), x must be −2. The input arrives 2 earlier.

misconception.wrong: y = f(x + 2) moves the graph 2 right

teach.heading: Coordinates after a translation
teach.note: Model.

model.problem: y = f(x) has a turning point at (3, −1). Find the turning point of y = f(x − 4) + 2.

teach.heading: Check: describe
teach.note: Show me on 3.

check.q: Which vector describes y = f(x) → y = f(x + 5)?
check.why: Inside the bracket moves horizontally in the opposite direction: 5 left. C is f(x) + 5.

practice: Write the vector for y = f(x) − 6
independent: Core: The point (2, 7) lies on y = f(x). Write the image on (a) y = f(x) + 4 (b) y = f(x − 1) (c) y = f(x + 3) − 2
Extend: Describe fully the transformation that maps y = x² onto y = x² + 6x + 9.
Stretch: y = x² − 8x + 10 is a translation of y = x². Find the translation vector by completing the square.
exit: Vector for y = f(x) + 7?
Vector for y = f(x − 3)?
Turning point (1, 4) on f. Where on y = f(x + 2)?
lessons.homework: 4MA1 Higher transformations of graphs: six questions on translations.
lessons.send: Support: tracing-paper style overlays (online graphing tool). Stretch: combined transformations.

lessons.unit: Unit 16: Harder graphs and transformations of graphs
lessons.title: Transformations of graphs: reflections and stretches
lessons.bigQuestion: What happens to a graph when we put a minus sign inside or outside the function?
objectives: Sketch y = af(x) and y = f(ax)
successCriteria: Reflect a graph in the x-axis or y-axis
Apply a vertical stretch y = 2f(x)
Apply a horizontal stretch y = f(2x) and find the image of a point
lessons.crossCurricular: Science: waves and their amplitude and frequency
lessons.smsc: Cultural: reflections and stretches in Islamic geometric art

keywords.def: a mirror image in a line
an enlargement in one direction only
how much the graph is stretched
a point that does not move

teach.heading: Reflections
bullets: f(−x): reflect in the y-axis, (x, y) → (−x, y)
teach.note: Show y = x³ − 3x: −f(x) and f(−x) happen to give the same graph (odd function).

teach.heading: Stretches
bullets: af(x): vertical stretch, scale factor a
teach.note: Inside again works 'backwards': f(2x) squashes horizontally by ½.

misconception.wrong: y = f(2x) stretches horizontally by scale factor 2
misconception.right: f(2x) is a horizontal stretch by scale factor ½

teach.heading: Images of points
bullets: Apply the rule to the coordinates
teach.note: Model.

model.problem: (4, 6) lies on y = f(x). Find its image on y = 3f(x), y = f(2x) and y = −f(x)

teach.heading: Check: which transformation?
teach.note: Show me on 3.

check.q: (2, −3) lies on y = f(x). Which point lies on y = f(−x)?
check.why: Reflect in the y-axis: x changes sign. A is −f(x); C changes both.

practice: (6, 2) lies on f. Image on y = f(3x)?
independent: Core: (3, 8) lies on y = f(x). Find its image on (a) y = −f(x) (b) y = f(−x) (c) y = ½f(x) (d) y = f(x/2)
Extend: The graph y = sin x (or any curve given) has a maximum at (90, 1). Find the maximum of y = 2f(x) and of y = f(2x).
Stretch: Describe the single transformation mapping y = x² onto y = 4x², and explain why it can be described as either a vertical or a horizontal stretch.
exit: What does y = −f(x) do?
(1, 5) on f. Image on y = f(−x)?
Scale factor of y = f(4x)?
lessons.homework: 4MA1 Higher: graph transformation sketches from the sheet, labelling images of the turning points.
lessons.send: Support: rule card (inside: x opposite; outside: y as written). Stretch: combined transformations.

lessons.title: Simultaneous linear equations by elimination
lessons.bigQuestion: How can two pieces of information pin down two unknowns?
objectives: Multiply one or both equations to match coefficients
successCriteria: Solve when a coefficient already matches
Solve after multiplying one equation
Solve after multiplying both equations and interpret graphically
lessons.crossCurricular: Business: two pricing equations; Science: two unknowns in chemistry
lessons.smsc: Moral: using two witnesses to establish truth (as in Islamic law)

keywords.def: two equations that are true at the same time
remove one unknown by adding or subtracting equations
the number in front of a letter
put a known value into an equation

starter: If x = 2, find y in x + y = 7

teach.heading: Same sign: subtract, different signs: add
bullets: Line up x, y and constants
teach.note: 3x + 2y = 16 and x + 2y = 8: subtract → 2x = 8, x = 4, then y = 2.

teach.heading: Multiplying to match
teach.note: Model.

teach.heading: Subtracting negatives
teach.note: Most errors happen here.

teach.heading: The graphical meaning
bullets: Each equation is a straight line
The solution is the intersection point
teach.note: Show both lines crossing at (7, −4) on a graphing tool.

teach.heading: Check: eliminate
teach.note: Show me on 3.

check.q: Solve x + y = 10 and x − y = 4
check.why: Add: 2x = 14, x = 7, y = 3. B swaps them; check both equations.

independent: Extend: Solve 5x − 2y = 24, 3x + 5y = 2
Stretch: 3 apples and 2 bananas cost £1.95; 2 apples and 5 bananas cost £2.40. Find the cost of each, then check.
exit: Solve x + 2y = 9, x − y = 3
What do you multiply to eliminate y in 2x + 3y = 7 and 5x − 2y = 8?
What does the solution represent on a graph?
lessons.homework: 4MA1 simultaneous equations practice: six questions including two word problems.
lessons.send: Support: SSS reminder and a column layout. Stretch: three equations, three unknowns.

lessons.title: Simultaneous equations by substitution and from contexts
lessons.bigQuestion: When is substitution quicker than elimination?
successCriteria: Solve when one equation gives y = …
Form and solve equations from a word problem
Choose the most efficient method and justify it
lessons.smsc: Social: fair pricing and transparent costs

keywords.def: replacing one variable with an expression for it
write equations from information
explain the meaning in context
using the fewest, simplest steps

starter: If y = 2x − 1, find y when x = 4

teach.heading: Substitution
teach.note: Model.

teach.heading: Choosing a method
bullets: Both in the form ax + by = c: elimination
teach.note: Sort five pairs by best method.

teach.heading: Forming equations
teach.note: Example: 4 adult and 3 child tickets cost £47; 2 adult and 5 child cost £41. Let a, c be prices in £: 4a + 3c = 47, 2a + 5c = 41 → a = 8, c = 5.

misconception.right: Adult tickets cost £8 and child tickets £5: answer in context

teach.heading: Check: which method?
teach.note: Show me on 3.

check.q: Best first step for x = 3y + 2 and 2x − 5y = 7?
check.why: x is already the subject, so substitute: 2(3y + 2) − 5y = 7 gives y = 3, x = 11.

practice: Form equations: two numbers sum to 30 and differ by 8
independent: Core: Solve (a) y = 3x − 5, x + y = 11 (b) x = 4 − y, 2x + 3y = 11
Extend: A cafe sells tea and coffee. 3 teas and 2 coffees cost £8.70; 2 teas and 3 coffees cost £9.30. Find the price of each.
Stretch: A two-digit number's digits add to 11. Reversing the digits increases the number by 27. Find the number.
exit: Solve y = 2x, x + y = 9
Form equations: 2 pens and a ruler cost £3.10; 1 pen and a ruler cost £2.20
Solve your equations
lessons.homework: 4MA1 problem-solving: four word problems leading to simultaneous equations.
lessons.send: Support: method decision card. Stretch: digit problems.

lessons.title: Simultaneous equations: one linear and one quadratic
lessons.bigQuestion: How many times can a straight line cross a curve?
objectives: Solve a linear and a quadratic equation simultaneously
Pair x and y values correctly
successCriteria: Solve y = x² and y = x + 6
Solve x² + y² = 25 and y = x + 1
Explain 0, 1 or 2 solutions using the discriminant or a sketch
lessons.crossCurricular: Physics: when a moving object reaches a curved path; Computing: collision detection in games

keywords.def: where two graphs meet
replace a variable with an expression
an x-value with its matching y-value
a line that touches a curve at exactly one point

teach.heading: Substitute the linear into the quadratic
bullets: Get a quadratic in one variable
Find the matching y for each x
teach.note: Model.

model.problem: Solve x² + y² = 25 and y = x + 1

teach.heading: Pairing values
bullets: Each x has its own y
Write the solutions as coordinate pairs
teach.note: The 4MA1 mark scheme requires correct pairs.

teach.heading: How many solutions?
teach.note: Answer the big question with sketches.

teach.heading: Check: solve
teach.note: Show me on 3.

check.q: Solve y = x² and y = x + 6
check.why: x² = x + 6, x² − x − 6 = 0, (x − 3)(x + 2) = 0. Then y = 9 or 4. C has the wrong signs; D swaps x and y.

practice: Solve x² + y² = 10 and y = x + 2
independent: Core: Solve (a) y = x² + 2x and y = x + 2 (b) x² + y² = 13 and y = x − 1
Extend: Solve 2x² − y² = 7 and y = x + 1 (give exact answers if needed).
Stretch: Find the value of c for which y = 2x + c is a tangent to y = x² + 3. Explain using the discriminant.
exit: Solve y = x² and y = 4
Solve y = x² − 2x and y = x
How many points does y = 5 meet y = x² + 7?
lessons.homework: 4MA1 Higher Paper 1H/2H past-paper style: three linear–quadratic simultaneous questions (5 marks each).
lessons.send: Support: substitution steps frame. Stretch: circles and tangents.
